\subsection{All lesson objectives (generated)}
\begin{longtable}{@{}p{1.5cm}p{0.72\linewidth}p{1.6cm}@{}}
\toprule Week & Objective & Goals\\ \midrule\endhead
\multicolumn{3}{@{}l}{\textbf{1: Robots Need Instructions}}\\
1.1 & The student can lay arrow cards in order so the parent robot walks from the start square to the star on the floor grid. & J1.G1\\
1.2 & The student can take turns laying and reading the cards, and say what each card will make the robot do. & J1.G6\\
1.3 & The student can find an arrow card in the wrong place and move it so the robot reaches the star. & J1.G4\\
1.4 & The student can say two of our rules: we use nicknames only, and we stop and ask a grown-up when an app asks for anything. & J1.G7\\
\midrule
\multicolumn{3}{@{}l}{\textbf{2: Meet Scratch}}\\
2.1 & The student can point to the sprite, the stage, the blocks and the green flag in Scratch. & J1.G2\\
2.2 & The student can snap a \enquote{when green flag clicked} script of three or four blocks so the cat talks, moves and makes a sound in order. & J1.G2\\
2.3 & The student can find a block that is not snapped on and fix it. & J1.G4\\
2.4 & The student can sit, hold the mouse and take screen breaks in a way that looks after their body and the Mac. & J1.G7\\
\midrule
\multicolumn{3}{@{}l}{\textbf{3: Bugs Are Clues}}\\
3.1 & The student can test a script, say what went wrong, change one thing and test again. & J1.G4\\
3.2 & The student can add a \enquote{wait 1 seconds} block so each step stays on the screen long enough to see. & J1.G2\\
3.3 & The student can spot steps in the wrong order, in a robot routine and in a script, and put them in the right order. & J1.G1, J1.G4\\
3.4 & The student can use kind words when a friend finds a bug in their work, or when they find a bug in a friend's work. & J1.G7\\
\midrule
\multicolumn{3}{@{}l}{\textbf{4: Repeat It!}}\\
4.1 & The student can build a repeat loop that runs the same blocks again, instead of snapping on the same blocks many times. & J1.G2\\
4.2 & The student can make a sprite dance or walk with \enquote{next costume} inside a repeat. & J1.G2\\
4.3 & The student can count how many times a loop runs and fix a repeat with too many or too few. & J1.G4\\
4.4 & The student can swap Driver and Helper when the timer runs out, and say what their loop does. & J1.G6, J1.G7\\
\midrule
\multicolumn{3}{@{}l}{\textbf{5: Play Day and Show Me}}\\
5.1 & The student can put arrow cards in order so a robot reaches the goal on an arrow maze. & J1.G1\\
5.2 & The student can build a green-flag script with a repeat loop that does something again. & J1.G2\\
5.3 & The student can find and fix a block that is not snapped on, in the wrong order or repeated the wrong number of times. & J1.G4\\
5.4 & The student can take turns as Driver and Helper and say what their script does. & J1.G6\\
\midrule
\multicolumn{3}{@{}l}{\textbf{6: When I Click\ldots}}\\
6.1 & The student can make a sprite act when it is clicked, using \enquote{when this sprite clicked}. & J1.G3\\
6.2 & The student can make a sprite walk and spin when a key is pressed, using \enquote{when key pressed} blocks. & J1.G3\\
6.3 & The student can find and fix a script that is under the wrong sprite or listens for the wrong key. & J1.G4\\
6.4 & The student can explain why our projects show nicknames and never real names or photos. & J1.G7\\
\midrule
\multicolumn{3}{@{}l}{\textbf{7: Two Sprites Talk}}\\
7.1 & The student can add a second sprite from the library and pick a backdrop. & J1.G2\\
7.2 & The student can give each sprite its own green-flag script and use wait so the two sprites take turns talking. & J1.G2, J1.G3\\
7.3 & The student can plan a tiny two-line conversation in two picture boxes and then build it. & J1.G5\\
7.4 & The student can say who made the sprites and backdrop they used and give them credit. & J1.G7\\
\midrule
\multicolumn{3}{@{}l}{\textbf{8: Draw With the Pen}}\\
8.1 & The student can walk a square on the floor and then make the cat draw it with pen down and repeat 4 of \enquote{move} and a quarter turn (90). & J1.G1, J1.G2\\
8.2 & The student can find and fix a turn that sits outside the repeat, so the cat draws all four sides. & J1.G4\\
8.3 & The student can say that a password is secret, like a toothbrush, and is never shared with friends. & J1.G7\\
8.4 & The student can choose who their greeting card will be for and draw one idea for it. & J1.G5\\
\midrule
\multicolumn{3}{@{}l}{\textbf{9: Project Studio}}\\
9.1 & The student can plan their greeting card on a three-box storyboard: start, middle and end. & J1.G5\\
9.2 & The student can build their card one storyboard box at a time, with the green flag, a repeat, a click or key event and a sound. & J1.G2, J1.G3, J1.G5\\
9.3 & The student can check a partner's card against the storyboard as Helper, and say what one of their own scripts does. & J1.G4, J1.G6\\
9.4 & The student can ask before showing someone else's work to other people. & J1.G7\\
\midrule
\multicolumn{3}{@{}l}{\textbf{10: Showcase and Certificate}}\\
10.1 & The student can show their greeting card and say what one script does, from the hat block down. & J1.G5, J1.G6\\
10.2 & The student can test their card with the green flag and with its click or key event, and fix a last-minute bug. & J1.G3, J1.G4\\
10.3 & The student can give kind sticker feedback on a friend's card and say which part they liked. & J1.G6, J1.G7\\
10.4 & The student can keep a showcase safe: family only, nicknames on screen. & J1.G7\\
\midrule
\multicolumn{3}{@{}l}{\textbf{B1: Unplugged Games Day}}\\
B1.1 & The student can guide a partner through an arrow maze with arrow cards in the right order, and use a repeat card to make the program shorter. & J1.G1\\
B1.2 & The student can color a pixel grid where each number stands for a color, and write a small number code for a partner. & J1.G1, J1.G2\\
B1.3 & The student can find and fix the bug on a detective card by acting the steps out. & J1.G4\\
B1.4 & The student can take turns as reader and robot and use kind words when a partner's steps have a bug. & J1.G6, J1.G7\\
\midrule
\multicolumn{3}{@{}l}{\textbf{B2: Remix Studio}}\\
B2.1 & The student can choose a past project and change it in two ways on purpose. & J1.G2\\
B2.2 & The student can add a click or key event to an old project so it does something new. & J1.G3\\
B2.3 & The student can find and fix a bug that a partner hid in their remix. & J1.G4\\
B2.4 & The student can say what they changed, and give credit when the idea came from someone else. & J1.G6, J1.G7\\
\midrule
\bottomrule\end{longtable}
